entities.name: West Indian manatee
entities.fact: West Indian manatees crowd into Florida's warm springs in winter because they cannot survive long in water below about 20 degrees Celsius.

entities.name: Wedgefish
entities.fact: Wedgefish are shark-like rays with a rounded, wedge-shaped snout, and many species are critically endangered because their fins are highly prized.

entities.name: Warty frogfish
entities.fact: The warty frogfish dangles a lure on a modified fin spine to tempt prey within reach of its huge mouth.

entities.name: Waspfish
entities.fact: Waspfish carry venomous dorsal spines and rest camouflaged against the seabed.

entities.name: Walleye pollock
entities.fact: Walleye pollock, sold as Alaska pollock, is among the world's largest fisheries by volume and is the usual fish in fish fingers and imitation crab.

entities.name: Western rock lobster
entities.fact: The western rock lobster is a spiny lobster of Western Australia that supports one of the country's most valuable fisheries.

entities.name: White hake
entities.fact: White hake is a long-bodied relative of the cod found over soft seabeds in the north-west Atlantic.

entities.name: Walking shark
entities.fact: Walking sharks wriggle across reef flats and tide pools on their paired fins, and can even cross short stretches of exposed reef.

entities.name: Wentletrap
entities.fact: Wentletraps are sea snails with ladder-like spiral shells, and the name comes from the Dutch word for a spiral staircase.

entities.name: Warty comb jelly
entities.fact: The warty comb jelly is a see-through, lobed predator that, carried in ships' ballast water, invaded the Black Sea in the 1980s.

entities.name: White-spotted jellyfish
entities.fact: The white-spotted jellyfish, native to the western Pacific, has spread to the Gulf of Mexico and elsewhere, where its blooms can clog fishing nets.

entities.name: Western wobbegong
entities.fact: The western wobbegong is a carpet shark of southern Western Australia whose fringed, mottled body camouflages it on the seabed.

entities.name: Western blue groper
entities.fact: The western blue groper is a very large wrasse of the reefs of southern Australia.

entities.name: Wrymouth
entities.fact: The wrymouth is an eel-like fish of the north-west Atlantic that lives in burrows in muddy seabed.

entities.name: Weasel shark
entities.fact: Weasel sharks are a family of slender sharks found along warm Indo-Pacific and West African coasts.

entities.name: White-spotted bamboo shark
entities.fact: The white-spotted bamboo shark is a small, slender Indo-Pacific reef shark that lays egg cases and is common in public aquariums.

entities.name: Whitetail dascyllus
entities.fact: The whitetail dascyllus shelters in small groups among branching corals on Indo-Pacific reefs.

entities.name: Winter skate
entities.fact: The winter skate of the north-west Atlantic has an eye-like spot on each wing and lives on sandy and gravelly seabeds.

entities.name: Lugworm
entities.fact: Lugworms live in U-shaped burrows in sand and mud, and leave coiled casts on the beach at low tide.

entities.name: Lamprey
entities.fact: Lampreys are jawless fish with a sucker mouth ringed with teeth, and several species fasten on to other fish to feed.

entities.name: Little penguin
entities.fact: The little penguin stands only about 30 centimetres tall and breeds along the southern coasts of Australia, including Phillip Island.

entities.name: Leatherjacket
entities.fact: Leatherjackets are a family of filefishes with tough, rough skin, found in warm and temperate seas.

entities.name: Lookdown
entities.fact: The lookdown has a steeply sloping, flattened forehead and a deep, silvery, disc-shaped body.

entities.name: Lined surgeonfish
entities.fact: The lined surgeonfish, also called the clown surgeonfish, defends grazing territories on shallow Indo-Pacific reefs with sharp spines at the base of its tail.

entities.name: Lyretail anthias
entities.fact: Lyretail anthias live in large shoals over reefs, and every fish starts life as a female, with the dominant ones later changing into males.

entities.name: Leopard coral grouper
entities.fact: The leopard coral grouper is a red, blue-spotted predator of the Great Barrier Reef and a major target of its reef fishery.

entities.name: Lollipop catshark
entities.fact: The lollipop catshark of the eastern Pacific has a broad rounded head and a thin tapering body and lives on the deep sea floor.

entities.name: Lion's paw scallop
entities.fact: The lion's paw scallop is a large, ridged scallop of the eastern Pacific, prized as seafood.

entities.name: Longbill spearfish
entities.fact: The longbill spearfish is a slender Atlantic billfish with a long, rounded bill.

entities.name: Lemon damselfish
entities.fact: The lemon damselfish is a bright yellow damselfish that shelters among branching corals on Indo-Pacific reefs.

entities.name: Palette surgeonfish
entities.fact: The palette surgeonfish, a bright blue Indo-Pacific reef fish, became famous as Dory in the film Finding Nemo.

entities.name: Pelican eel
entities.fact: The pelican eel, or gulper eel, has a vast pouch-like mouth on a thin body and lives in the deep sea, where it has been filmed ballooning its head.

entities.name: Painted frogfish
entities.fact: The painted frogfish can alter its colour over time to match its surroundings and lures prey with a fishing-rod-like spine.

entities.name: Pacific sea nettle
entities.fact: The Pacific sea nettle is a large, long-armed jellyfish of the north-eastern Pacific with a golden-brown bell.

entities.name: Purple-striped jellyfish
entities.fact: The purple-striped jellyfish of Monterey Bay feeds on other jellyfish, especially moon jellies.

entities.name: Pacific blackdragon
entities.fact: Female Pacific blackdragons have a light-tipped chin barbel and rows of light organs along the body, while the males are tiny and toothless.

entities.name: Pacific viperfish
entities.fact: The Pacific viperfish has fang-like teeth so long that they curve outside its closed mouth.

entities.name: Pacific hagfish
entities.fact: The Pacific hagfish defends itself by releasing slime that swells into a choking gel in seawater.

entities.name: Paper nautilus
entities.fact: Female paper nautiluses, which are in fact octopuses, make a thin papery egg case that they carry with them.

entities.name: Pacific ocean perch
entities.fact: The Pacific ocean perch is a long-lived rockfish that can reach many decades of age.

entities.name: Patagonian squid
entities.fact: The Patagonian squid is a major catch in the waters around the Falkland Islands.

entities.name: Phantom jelly
entities.fact: The phantom jelly is a rarely seen deep-sea giant with ribbon-like oral arms that can stretch up to about 10 metres.

entities.name: Pajama cardinalfish
entities.fact: Male pajama cardinalfish incubate the fertilised eggs in their mouths.

entities.name: Magellanic penguin
entities.fact: Magellanic penguins breed in huge colonies along the coasts of Argentina, Chile and the Falkland Islands.

entities.name: Magnificent sea anemone
entities.fact: The magnificent sea anemone is a favourite host of clownfish on Indo-Pacific reefs.

entities.name: Manefish
entities.fact: Manefish are deep-sea fish with a tall, mane-like dorsal fin, and they are sometimes found close to siphonophores and jellyfish.

entities.name: Molly miller
entities.fact: The molly miller is a small blenny that lives in tide pools and on shallow rocky shores of the Atlantic.

entities.name: Mosshead warbonnet
entities.fact: The mosshead warbonnet is a small north Pacific fish with a crest of branching, moss-like tentacles on its head.

entities.name: Morwong
entities.fact: Morwongs are a family of reef fish of the Southern Hemisphere, caught commercially and by anglers off Australia and New Zealand.

entities.name: Mulloway
entities.fact: The mulloway is a large, silvery Australian fish, long prized by anglers, that can grow to well over a metre.

entities.name: Maori octopus
entities.fact: The Maori octopus is a large octopus of New Zealand and southern Australian waters.

entities.name: Short-beaked common dolphin
entities.fact: Short-beaked common dolphins carry an hourglass pattern of grey, yellow and white on their sides and often gather in very large, fast-moving pods.

entities.name: Sato's beaked whale
entities.fact: Sato's beaked whale is a rarely seen North Pacific species that was only formally described as new to science in 2019.

entities.name: Burrunan dolphin
entities.fact: The Burrunan dolphin lives in sheltered bays and lakes of southern Australia, such as Port Phillip Bay and the Gippsland Lakes.

entities.name: Bottlenose whale
entities.fact: Bottlenose whales of the genus Hyperoodon are deep-diving beaked whales with a rounded, bulbous forehead.

entities.name: Spotted dolphin
entities.fact: Spotted dolphins are born plain and gradually develop their spots as they age.

entities.name: Squalodon
entities.fact: Squalodon was an extinct toothed whale of the Oligocene and Miocene with triangular, serrated-edged teeth, and its name means shark tooth.

entities.name: Shortfin mako
entities.fact: Shortfin makos keep their bodies warmer than the surrounding water, which powers their famous bursts of speed.

entities.name: White shark
entities.fact: The white shark, better known as the great white, can sense the faint electrical fields given off by the muscles of hidden prey.

entities.name: Speartooth shark
entities.fact: The speartooth shark is a rare river shark of northern Australia and Papua New Guinea that moves between rivers, estuaries and the sea.

entities.name: Sevengill shark
entities.fact: Sevengill sharks have seven pairs of gill slits where most sharks have five.

entities.name: Smalleye pygmy shark
entities.fact: The smalleye pygmy shark is one of the smallest sharks alive, a deep-water species of the Indo-Pacific that stays under 25 centimetres long.

entities.name: Spadenose shark
entities.fact: The spadenose shark is a small shark of Indo-Pacific coasts, caught in large numbers by local fisheries.

entities.name: Sliteye shark
entities.fact: The sliteye shark is a slim requiem shark of Indo-Pacific shallows with large, slit-like eyes.

entities.name: Southern sleeper shark
entities.fact: The southern sleeper shark is a large, slow-moving shark of cold southern waters that has been recorded at depths of more than a kilometre.

entities.name: Taillight shark
entities.fact: The taillight shark is a rarely seen, small deep-water shark with light-producing organs, and only a handful of specimens are known.

entities.name: Whiskery shark
entities.fact: The whiskery shark is a slender, bottom-feeding shark of southern Australia named for the barbels beside its nostrils.

entities.name: Whaler shark
entities.fact: Whaler shark is the Australian name for sharks of the genus Carcharhinus, which includes bull, blacktip and bronze whalers.

entities.name: Snaggletooth shark
entities.fact: The snaggletooth shark has long, hooked, serrated teeth that protrude from its mouth even when it is closed.

entities.name: Smooth dogfish
entities.fact: The smooth dogfish is a small shark of the western Atlantic that crushes crabs and lobsters with flat, pavement-like teeth.

entities.name: Atolla jellyfish
entities.fact: When attacked, the Atolla jellyfish flashes a swirling ring of blue light, a burglar alarm that may attract predators of its attacker.

entities.name: Black seadevil
entities.fact: Female black seadevils dangle a glowing lure in the dark depths and are far larger than the males.

entities.name: Blob sculpin
entities.fact: The blob sculpin is a soft, gelatinous-looking fish of the deep north-east Pacific that is often mistaken for the blobfish.

entities.name: Giant ostracod
entities.fact: Giant ostracods are shrimp-like crustaceans inside a bean-shaped shell, up to a few centimetres long, that hunt in the dark deep sea.

entities.name: Gonate squid
entities.fact: Brooding female gonate squid of the species Gonatus onyx carry their eggs in their arms for months at depth.

entities.name: Bathysaurus
entities.fact: Bathysaurus is a genus of large deep-sea lizardfish that wait on the seabed to ambush prey.

entities.name: Bone-eating worm
entities.fact: Bone-eating worms of the genus Osedax use acid-secreting, root-like tissue to digest the bones of dead whales on the seafloor.

entities.name: Pygmy blue whale
entities.fact: The pygmy blue whale, a subspecies of the blue whale in the Indian Ocean and South Pacific, is shorter overall and has a proportionally shorter tail section than other blues.

entities.name: Antarctic blue whale
entities.fact: The Antarctic blue whale is the largest subspecies of the blue whale and was hunted to a tiny fraction of its former numbers.

entities.name: Pygmy beaked whale
entities.fact: The pygmy beaked whale is one of the smallest beaked whales and was first described from Peruvian waters in the early 1990s.

entities.name: Pygmy Bryde's whale
entities.fact: The pygmy Bryde's whale, now often called Eden's whale, is a small baleen whale of warm Indo-Pacific coastal waters.

entities.name: White whale
entities.fact: White whale is another name for the beluga, whose calves are born dark grey and turn white as they reach adulthood.

entities.name: Greenland right whale
entities.fact: Greenland right whale is an old name for the bowhead, an Arctic giant that can live for around two centuries.

entities.name: Giant beaked whale
entities.fact: The giant beaked whale, also known as Baird's beaked whale, is the largest of the beaked whales, reaching about 12 metres.

entities.name: Southern four-toothed whale
entities.fact: The southern four-toothed whale is a large beaked whale of cold southern seas, named for the two pairs of teeth at the tip of its lower jaw.

entities.name: Little piked whale
entities.fact: Little piked whale is an old name for the minke, one of the smallest of the great rorqual whales.

entities.name: Western gray whale
entities.fact: The western gray whale, a population of the north-west Pacific, is critically endangered, with only a few hundred animals left.

entities.name: Indo-Pacific beaked whale
entities.fact: The Indo-Pacific beaked whale was known for decades only from two skulls and is still one of the rarest large whales.

entities.name: Tasman beaked whale
entities.fact: The Tasman beaked whale keeps a full set of functional teeth in both jaws, unlike most beaked whales.

entities.name: Bering Sea beaked whale
entities.fact: The Bering Sea beaked whale lives in the cold North Pacific and is rarely seen at sea.

entities.name: Chilean blue whale
entities.fact: Chilean blue whales feed in the Gulf of Corcovado and nearby waters of southern Chile, an important feeding area for the species.

entities.name: Atlantic gray whale
entities.fact: The Atlantic gray whale once lived on both sides of the North Atlantic and was hunted to extinction by about the 1700s.

entities.name: Eastern North Pacific gray whale
entities.fact: Eastern North Pacific gray whales make one of the longest migrations of any mammal, travelling roughly 16,000 kilometres or more between Alaska and Baja California.

entities.name: Ophthalmosaurus
entities.fact: Ophthalmosaurus was a dolphin-shaped Jurassic ichthyosaur with some of the largest eyes, relative to body size, of any known vertebrate.

entities.name: Nothosaurus
entities.fact: Nothosaurus was a long-necked, fish-eating marine reptile of the Triassic that probably hunted in shallow seas and rested on shores.

entities.name: Cymbospondylus
entities.fact: Cymbospondylus was a very large, eel-like early ichthyosaur of the Triassic, reaching roughly nine metres in length.

entities.name: Hesperornis
entities.fact: Hesperornis was a flightless, toothed seabird of the Cretaceous that swam with powerful legs.

entities.name: Platecarpus
entities.fact: Platecarpus was a streamlined mid-sized mosasaur of the Late Cretaceous seas of North America and Europe.

entities.name: Thalassomedon
entities.fact: Thalassomedon was a long-necked plesiosaur of the Cretaceous Western Interior Seaway whose neck made up roughly half of its body length.

entities.name: Cryptoclidus
entities.fact: Cryptoclidus was a medium-sized, long-necked plesiosaur of Jurassic Europe with many interlocking, needle-like teeth.

entities.name: Rhomaleosaurus
entities.fact: Rhomaleosaurus was a short-necked, big-headed plesiosaur of Early Jurassic Europe, around seven metres long.

entities.name: Hainosaurus
entities.fact: Hainosaurus was a giant mosasaur of the Late Cretaceous, named after the Hainaut region of Belgium where its fossils were found.

entities.name: Ptychodus
entities.fact: Ptychodus was a Cretaceous shark with flat, ridged, pavement-like teeth suited to crushing hard-shelled prey.

entities.name: Squalicorax
entities.fact: Squalicorax, the crow shark, was a Cretaceous shark whose serrated teeth are found with the bones of the marine reptiles and other animals it scavenged.

entities.name: Edestus
entities.fact: Edestus was a Carboniferous relative of sharks known for long, serrated teeth set in curved rows.

entities.name: Hybodus
entities.fact: Hybodus was an early shark relative of Triassic to Cretaceous seas that carried a spine in front of each dorsal fin.

entities.name: Bothriolepis
entities.fact: Bothriolepis was a Devonian armoured placoderm fish with jointed bony pectoral fins, and its fossils are found on many continents.

entities.name: Pikaia
entities.fact: Pikaia is a Cambrian worm-like animal from the Burgess Shale that had a primitive stiffening rod and is thought to be an early relative of vertebrates.

entities.name: Wiwaxia
entities.fact: Wiwaxia was a Cambrian seafloor grazer from the Burgess Shale covered in overlapping scales and two rows of spines.

entities.name: Marrella
entities.fact: Marrella is one of the most common fossils of the Cambrian Burgess Shale, an arthropod with long, backward-pointing head spines.

entities.name: Cameroceras
entities.fact: Cameroceras was an Ordovician nautiloid with a straight, cone-shaped shell that may have been several metres long.

entities.name: Shastasaurus
entities.fact: Shastasaurus was a large, slender-snouted ichthyosaur of the Late Triassic, named after Shasta County in California.

entities.name: Temnodontosaurus
entities.fact: Temnodontosaurus was a large Early Jurassic ichthyosaur, around nine metres long, with some of the biggest eyes of any known vertebrate.

entities.name: Dakosaurus
entities.fact: Dakosaurus was a Jurassic sea crocodile relative with a short, deep skull and serrated teeth, and one species was nicknamed Godzilla.

entities.name: Desmostylus
entities.fact: Desmostylus was a bulky, hippo-like marine mammal of Miocene North Pacific coasts whose teeth were built from bundled columns.

entities.name: Odobenocetops
entities.fact: Odobenocetops was a Pliocene whale from the coasts of Peru and Chile with a walrus-like face and two tusks, one far longer than the other in males.

entities.name: Tully monster
entities.fact: The Tully monster was a soft-bodied animal about 30 centimetres long with eyes on stalks, known from Illinois fossils, and its place in the tree of life has long been debated.

entities.name: Giant manta ray
entities.fact: The giant manta ray can span about 7 metres across and was listed as endangered in 2020 because of fishing for its gill plates.

entities.name: Pacific Ocean
entities.fact: The Pacific Ocean covers about 165 million square kilometres, more than all of Earth's land combined, making it the largest and deepest ocean.

entities.name: Mauna Kea
entities.fact: Measured from its base on the Pacific seabed to its summit, Mauna Kea in Hawaii rises about 10,200 metres, taller than Everest above sea level.

entities.name: Seawise Giant
entities.fact: Seawise Giant, later renamed Knock Nevis, was the longest ship ever built, at about 458 metres from bow to stern.

entities.name: Ahmed Gabr
entities.fact: Egyptian diver Ahmed Gabr set the scuba depth record in 2014, descending to 332.35 metres in the Red Sea off Dahab.

entities.name: Gertrude Ederle
entities.fact: In 1926 Gertrude Ederle became the first woman to swim the English Channel, finishing in about 14 hours 39 minutes, faster than any man before her.

entities.name: Shark Bay seagrass
entities.fact: The Posidonia australis meadow in Shark Bay, Western Australia, is the largest known plant in the world, covering about 180 square kilometres and some 4,500 years old.

entities.name: Typhoon-class submarine
entities.fact: Soviet Typhoon-class submarines, about 175 metres long and roughly 48,000 tonnes submerged, are the largest submarines ever built.

entities.name: Vestas Sailrocket 2
entities.fact: Vestas Sailrocket 2 set the world sailing speed record in 2012, reaching about 65 knots, or roughly 121 kilometres per hour, off Walvis Bay in Namibia.

entities.name: Mid-ocean ridge
entities.fact: The mid-ocean ridge is a continuous chain of underwater mountains, about 65,000 kilometres long, making it the longest mountain range on Earth.

entities.name: Seep tubeworm
entities.fact: Seep tubeworms living around cold seeps in the Gulf of Mexico have been aged at over 250 years, making them among the longest-lived animals known.
